newsitem.title: FRANCE: GREEK PRESIDENT SAYS TURKEY ENDANGERS PEACE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PRESIDENT SAYS TURKEY ENDANGERS PEACE.

text.p: Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos accused Turkey on Monday of endangering peace in southern Europe and refusing to respect international law.

Peaceful coexistence "is threatened by the systematic refusal...of Turkey to accept international law...to the extent of making open threats of war in resolutions by its national assembly," he told the 40-nation Council of Europe.

He pointed to territorial disputes over islands in the Aegean Sea and over Cyprus, divided since Turkish troops invaded in 1974 and occupied its northern third after a coup attempt in Nicosia engineered by a military junta then ruling Greece.
Last year, the two countries came close to war over rights to two uninhabited islets in the eastern Aegean.

Stephanopoulos, addressing the parliamentary assembly of the Council of Europe, urged Turkey to grant the Greek minority in Istanbul the same rights he said the Moslem minority enjoyed in Thrace, Greece.
Some Turkish parliamentarians at the Council of Europe, which safeguards democracy and human rights across the continent, expressed irritation at Stephanopoulos' remarks.
"It is a shame to have to listen to such declarations when relations between Greece and Turkey have entered a positive phase," said Cevdet Akcali.
